summary: Rabbi Soffer teaches from the Hafes Hayim on the laws of Shemirat HaLashon, beginning with how fathers guide their young children against speaking Lashon Hara. He explains seven criteria that permit revealing when someone stole, damaged, or insulted another person, including rebuking the person softly first and having pure intent for toelet. He also discusses why a person who is himself guilty of similar wrongdoings cannot speak about another, citing the story of Yehu and Bet Ahav.
questions: How should a parent handle young children when they speak Lashon Hara?
What are the rules about repeating things told in confidence?
When is one permitted to reveal that someone stole or caused damage?
What seven criteria are needed before telling someone about damage another person caused them?
Can a person who commits the same wrongdoings speak out about someone else?
